comments.content: The embedded ledger block is not invisible in the rendered summary. `EncodeLedger` emits `<!-- ocr-ledger -->\n{json}\n<!-- /ocr-ledger -->`, and the opening marker line is a self-terminated HTML comment, so per CommonMark HTML-block rules the JSON payload lines that follow are ordinary markdown paragraphs and render as visible text (the same reason the summary content after `<!-- ocr-summary -->` is visible). Every run with `--resolution-tracking` therefore displays raw machine state (`{"version":1,...}` with run tags, paths, and finding snippets) to human readers, contradicting design D1, whose stated rationale for the HTML-comment approach is "invisible in rendered Markdown". The fix belongs in `format.EncodeLedger` (parse/strip in `format.StripLedger`/`ParseLedger` must follow): emit the payload inside one self-contained comment — e.g. a single line `<!-- ocr-ledger {\"version\":1,...} -->`, or open the comment without a same-line `-->` and close it after the payload so the JSON lines stay inside the HTML block. The same embedding is done by `trackedNoIssuesBody` in internal/publish/ledger.go.
